edited_fraction: construction: 0.42% of nanoTabPFN's 3.7M weights non-zero; repair: 125 tensors / ~105 million entries of TabPFN-3.5 (fraction unclear)
cost_reported: wall-clock only: repair session 62 min (of 5 h budget); KV-cache programs 19.6 and 70.3 min; no baseline time comparison
evidence_notes: WSP on tabular foundation models is the whole paper (p.1-5). In construction, Astra writes nanoTabPFN's weights through Python blocks run by the harness, with no data and no forward passes (p.3, App. A p.9), i.e. open loop; the TabPFN-3.5 repair uses activations, validation feedback and closed-form ridge/least-squares solves to set weights (p.14-15), so both protocols and partly solver_delegated. Success criteria were 'fixed before the run' (p.15) but no registry or timestamp is given, so prereg is coded none; nanoTabPFN reports the better of two sessions and the repair one session (p.10, p.15), so multiple_runs is coded no. TabPFN-3.5's total size is not stated (the repair alone changes ~105M entries), so target_params_max is null.
